agenda: Threats to international peace and security
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objective is to place the Russian Federation’s complaint regarding military-biological activities in Ukraine on the Council’s formal agenda, force the United States and Ukraine to provide clarifications, and frame the issue as a matter of BWC compliance rather than disinformation. The main difficulty will be overcoming Western objections to any reference to the Russian complaint; we have therefore avoided naming states or establishing an investigative commission, aiming to attract at least nine votes while preventing a P3 veto.
steps.text:
The Security Council,
Reaffirming the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,
Recalling the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on their Destruction of 1972,
Reaffirming that the use, development, production, acquisition, stockpiling, or retention of biological weapons constitutes a threat to international peace and security,
Noting with concern that allegations of non-compliance with the Convention, including those relating to military-biological activities, have been brought to the attention of the Security Council,
Emphasizing the importance of full compliance with the Convention by all States Parties,
Stressing the need for all States Parties to resolve any concerns regarding compliance through consultation and cooperation in accordance with the Convention,
Taking note of the complaint submitted by the Russian Federation under Article VI of the Convention,
Having considered the complaint,
1. Calls upon all States Parties to the Convention to fully comply with their obligations under the Convention;
2. Takes note of the complaint submitted by the Russian Federation and of other relevant communications regarding allegations of non-compliance with the Convention;
3. Requests the Secretary-General to seek clarifications from all States Parties concerned regarding any allegations of non-compliance with the Convention, including those relating to military-biological activities, and to report to the Security Council within 90 days;
4. Encourages all States Parties to engage in bilateral and multilateral consultations to resolve any concerns regarding compliance with the Convention, in accordance with Article V of the Convention;
5. Decides to remain seized of the matter.

messages.Albania: Albania supports full compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention, but it cannot support a text that legitimizes the Russian Federation's unsubstantiated complaint. We ask that PP7 and PP8 be deleted, OP2 be neutralized, and a new operative paragraph be added calling on all States Parties to refrain from disinformation. Unless these changes are made, Albania will abstain on the draft.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports a technical, non-politicized follow-up that helps clarify BWC compliance concerns through the Convention's own procedures. We can support the text with amendments that anonymize the Article VI complaint, ensure the Secretary-General's clarification process is impartial and coordinated with the BWC Implementation Support Unit, and reaffirm that Council action does not prejudge attribution or States Parties' rights. Brazil would not support any move to establish an ad hoc investigative mechanism outside the Convention's procedures.
messages.China: China supports the Russian Federation's draft as a constructive effort to promote BWC compliance and address allegations through dialogue and consultation. We propose balanced amendments to avoid prejudging allegations, ensure that the Secretary-General's clarifications are objective, impartial and fully consult concerned States Parties, and reaffirm that compliance concerns should not be politicized. China will support the text if these changes are reflected.
messages.France: France cannot support this draft, which is not a genuine BWC compliance initiative but a politicized attempt to lend credibility to unsubstantiated allegations. The appropriate framework for such concerns is the Biological Weapons Convention, not the Security Council. France will vote against the text as drafted; at a minimum, OP3, PP4's reference to military-biological activities, PP7 and OP2 would have to be removed.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports full compliance with the BWC, but the current draft risks lending Security Council weight to allegations without verified evidence and bypassing the Convention’s own consultative framework. We ask the penholder to affirm the BWC’s primacy, neutralize OP2, and ensure any Secretary-General reporting is factual, consultative and non-duplicative. Without these changes, Gabon will abstain.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports full compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention and the peaceful resolution of compliance concerns through the Convention’s procedures. The current text should explicitly avoid prejudging the merits of any allegation and should ensure that any Secretary-General follow-up is inclusive, balanced and consistent with Articles V and VI. With the changes above, Ghana could support the draft.
messages.India: India supports full compliance with the BWC and believes compliance concerns should be addressed through the Convention’s consultative mechanisms, without politicization. We can support this draft if the Secretary-General’s role is limited to facilitating information exchange and reporting on consensus, and if the text is balanced and does not prejudge the upcoming BWC Review Conference. We also ask that the preamble acknowledge all relevant communications, not only one complaint.
messages.Ireland: Ireland supports full compliance with the BWC and fact-based resolution of compliance concerns, but the current text risks politicising the Convention and lending credibility to unsubstantiated allegations. We ask the penholder to remove the Russian-specific references and the 'military-biological activities' language, and to frame any Secretary-General role as facilitative and without prejudice to Articles V and VI. These changes are necessary for Ireland to be able to support the text.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the Biological Weapons Convention and the principle that compliance concerns should be resolved through consultation and cooperation, not politicized in the Council. As drafted, the text prejudges a complaint and risks duplicating or undermining the Convention’s own processes, so Kenya would abstain on the current text. We ask the penholder to make the references to communications generic, require any Secretary-General follow-up to rest on credible and substantiated information and coordinate with BWC mechanisms, and add a reference to the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the objectives of the Biological Weapons Convention and believes that compliance concerns must be addressed through cooperative, non-discriminatory procedures under the Convention. The current text should not single out one complaint or imply a Security Council judgment, and it must fully preserve the central role of the BWC and its upcoming Review Conference. Mexico can support a balanced text that facilitates Article V consultations and avoids politicization; without these changes, we would have serious difficulty supporting the draft.
messages.Norway: Norway strongly supports the Biological Weapons Convention and transparency, but cannot support language that singles out or appears to validate a particular national complaint. We ask that references to the Russian Federation’s Article VI complaint be made neutral and that the Secretary-General’s role remain within the Convention, based on information provided by States Parties and without creating an investigative mechanism. With those changes, Norway can support the text.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports full compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention and constructive dialogue, but the current text risks politicizing the Council's consideration by focusing on one Member State's complaint. To be in a position to support, we ask that the references to the Russian Federation's complaint be made neutral, that OP3 be clearly anchored in the Convention and based on credible information, and that the Council preserve consensus. Otherwise, the UAE will abstain.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this draft. It is not a genuine BWC compliance initiative but an attempt to legitimise unsubstantiated Russian allegations and to draw the Security Council into a disinformation exercise. Any genuine concerns must be pursued through the Biological Weapons Convention's own Article V procedures, not through a Security Council-mandated clarifications process. We therefore ask the penholder to withdraw the text; absent that, these red-line deletions would be the minimum necessary.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft. It takes note of and effectively validates the Russian Federation’s unsubstantiated complaint and tasks the Secretary-General with pursuing allegations that are better addressed through the BWC’s established procedures. We require deletion of PP4, PP7, PP8, OP2 and OP3; any text we could consider must be neutral and must not lend Council credibility to disinformation.

steps.summary: The revised text removes the Russian-specific complaint and the Secretary-General clarifications mandate, replacing them with neutral BWC compliance and Article V language. This should secure broad support among non-permanent members while avoiding a negative vote from any permanent member, although several Western members may abstain.

messages.Albania: Albania welcomes the removal of the targeted references and the neutralization of OP2, and we can support the text with one remaining important change. OP3 should explicitly address disinformation and unsubstantiated allegations concerning biological weapons rather than retaining the vague reference to 'double standards'. This would prevent the draft from being used to legitimize false narratives and would uphold the Council's credibility.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the current text as it stands. We welcome the revisions that anonymize references to the complaint and reinforce Article V consultations and the centrality of the Ninth Review Conference. The text rightly avoids prejudging attribution or duplicating the Convention's processes, and Brazil calls on all States Parties to comply fully with the BWC and to resolve concerns through the Convention's consensus-based mechanisms.
messages.China: China thanks the Russian Federation for revising the text to neutralize the allegations and to include clear language against politicization and double standards. The current text upholds the Biological Weapons Convention, respects Article V consultations, and avoids duplicating the Convention’s processes, which China supports. China does not insist on a new Security Council-mandated clarification mechanism and can support the text as it stands. We encourage all States Parties to provide timely and objective clarifications through the Convention.
messages.France: France welcomes the revisions to the draft, which now focus on the Biological Weapons Convention and avoid politicized or unsubstantiated allegations. We can support the current text as it stands. Compliance concerns must be addressed through the Convention’s procedures and the Ninth Review Conference.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the revised text. It affirms the centrality of the Biological Weapons Convention, encourages Article V consultations, and avoids prejudging allegations before the appropriate forum. We appreciate the penholder's willingness to neutralize the references and can support the draft as it stands.
messages.Ghana: Ghana remains committed to the BWC and supports Article V consultations, but the current text still lacks a balanced, non-discriminatory mechanism to clarify compliance allegations. Our red line is a Secretary-General reporting clause that treats all allegations equally and does not prejudge their merits. Without that, Ghana cannot support the draft and will abstain.
messages.India: India appreciates the removal of singling out and the inclusion of Review Conference language. While India had proposed a Secretary-General information-exchange role, it can accept the BWC-centered framework if OP3 is balanced and fact-based. India asks that OP3 avoid 'unfounded accusations' and instead call for impartial, fact-based and transparent consideration of any allegations; with that, India can support the text.
messages.Ireland: Ireland welcomes the removal of targeted references and the reaffirmation of the Convention’s procedures; the text is now much closer to a balanced BWC-focused statement. We can support it if a neutral, time-bound follow-up is added: a request for the Secretary-General to seek clarifications from concerned States Parties and report back within 90 days, without prejudice to Articles V and VI. This preserves the Council’s role while respecting the Convention and avoids prejudging the facts.
messages.Kenya: Kenya supports the Biological Weapons Convention and the Ninth Review Conference as the proper forum for compliance concerns. We appreciate the generic communications language and the reference to the Review Conference. However, given the lack of consensus and the risk of politicizing the Convention, Kenya will abstain on the current text.
messages.Mexico: Mexico supports the revised text as it stands. We welcome the neutralization of references to the complaint and the explicit confirmation that the Ninth Review Conference is the appropriate forum, which were our core concerns. We consider that the text preserves the Convention's own procedures and does not prejudge the merits of any allegation, and we have no further requests.
messages.Norway: Norway supports the revised text. It reaffirms the BWC, avoids singling out any State Party, and correctly defers compliance concerns to the Convention’s procedures and the Ninth Review Conference without establishing an investigative mechanism. Norway will vote in favour.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE thanks the penholder for the revised text and welcomes the neutralization of references and the anti-politicization language. While the text is balanced, we remain concerned that Security Council action on BWC compliance could duplicate or prejudge the Convention's own processes, especially ahead of the Ninth Review Conference. For these reasons, the UAE will abstain on the current text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks the penholder for revising the text to remove targeted references and to place compliance firmly within the BWC framework. We can support the current draft as it stands. We stress that the Security Council should not duplicate or prejudge the Convention's consensus-based processes, and we look to all States Parties to uphold the BWC and avoid unfounded accusations.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this text. We welcome the deletion of targeted references, but the remaining language still attempts to direct compliance concerns away from the Security Council and lends credibility to unfounded accusations. We require the red-line changes above, including an explicit savings clause for the Council's Charter authority; otherwise we will vote against.

steps.summary: The revision accepts all US red lines by deleting the communications paragraph and OP3, revising PP7/PP8, and adding a savings clause; a neutral fact-based preambular reference addresses India's concerns. It retains BWC-centered Article V consultations and the Ninth Review Conference while rejecting new Security Council-mandated clarification mechanisms. The draft is expected to pass with 10 votes in favour, no negative votes, and 5 abstentions.
steps.text:
The Security Council,

Reaffirming the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,

Recalling the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on their Destruction of 1972,

Reaffirming that the use, development, production, acquisition, stockpiling, or retention of biological weapons constitutes a threat to international peace and security,

Emphasizing the importance of full compliance with the Convention by all States Parties,

Stressing the need for all States Parties to resolve any concerns regarding compliance through consultation and cooperation in accordance with the Convention,

Stressing the need for all States Parties to consider any allegations of non-compliance impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, and to uphold the authority of the Convention,

Recalling that the Convention provides the appropriate framework for addressing compliance concerns, including through Article V consultations, while reaffirming the Security Council's primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security under the Charter of the United Nations,

Welcoming the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties to the Convention,

1. Calls upon all States Parties to the Convention to fully comply with their obligations under the Convention;

2. Encourages all States Parties to engage in bilateral and multilateral consultations to resolve any concerns regarding compliance with the Convention, in accordance with Article V of the Convention, including, as appropriate, through a consultative meeting of States Parties;

3. Reaffirms that the Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties to the Convention is an appropriate forum to consider issues of compliance and verification, and that consideration of this matter by the Security Council is without prejudice to the work of the Review Conference and to the procedures set out in the Convention;

4. Affirms that nothing in this resolution shall be construed to limit or prejudge the Security Council's authority under the Charter of the United Nations to address threats to international peace and security, including alleged non-compliance with the Convention;

5. Decides to remain seized of the matter.

reasons.Albania: Albania shares the draft’s formal support for the BWC but will not endorse a Russian-initiated text it views as politicized and lacking language against disinformation; abstention aligns with its pro-Western stance without opposing the Convention itself.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil's last negotiation position was support with no requested changes, and the BWC-centred text aligns with Brazil's long-standing commitment to the Convention and multilateral disarmament. No new element in the final draft justified shifting to abstention or opposition.
reasons.China: China supported the Russian draft in negotiations and generally favours a non-targeted, BWC-centred text that avoids politicization while preserving Security Council authority. A yes vote is consistent with China’s prior positions and its support for the Russian Federation’s initiative.
reasons.France: France’s stated position in the last negotiation round was support, and the draft’s focus on BWC compliance aligns with France’s non-proliferation priorities. No changes were requested, so France votes in favour.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon abstained on the Russian-drafted biological weapons resolution on 2 November 2022. There is no indication Gabon spoke before the vote.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana supports the BWC and compliance but had a red-line request for a balanced clarification mechanism, which was rejected; abstention reflects its preference for impartial, non-politicized multilateral processes rather than opposing the resolution outright.
reasons.India: India’s key request for an operative provision against politicization and double standards was not retained, and it is wary of supporting a contested, politicized draft while remaining committed to the BWC. India thus abstains rather than votes against.
reasons.Ireland: Ireland historically abstained on the Russian BWC draft, preferring that compliance concerns be handled through the Convention and its Review Conference rather than a politicised Council process. Its rejected amendment reinforces that its abstention reflected process and substance concerns, not opposition to the Convention.
reasons.Kenya: Kenya abstained on the Russian BWC draft because it was not the product of inclusive consultations and risked politicizing the Convention rather than strengthening it; consistent with Council practice, Kenya did not speak before the vote.
reasons.Mexico: Mexico abstained, consistent with its preference for addressing BWC compliance through the Convention’s own mechanisms and the Review Conference rather than a politicized Council process; it did not take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Norway: Norway is a strong supporter of the BWC and multilateral verification, but it would not support a Russian-initiated text that Western partners viewed as a distraction from genuine compliance concerns. Abstaining aligns with Norway’s multilateralist stance while avoiding endorsement of the draft’s political framing.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor and a permanent member, Russia supports its own draft and would speak in favour to present it as a constructive, consensus-oriented text. The statement reinforces Russia’s emphasis on the BWC and its opposition to politicization.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE supported the earlier BWC-related resolution by consensus but in this vote, consistent with its stated negotiation position, it abstained to avoid politicization and affirm the Convention's own review and consultation mechanisms.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom voted against this Russian-drafted BWC text on 2 November 2022, viewing it as a disinformation-driven distraction rather than a credible effort to strengthen the Convention. Supporting the BWC through its proper review processes, not this Council initiative, aligned with UK policy and alliance positions.
reasons.United States of America: The United States at this date opposed Russia’s BWC draft as a disinformation exercise and voted against it; as a permanent member, its negative vote prevents adoption.

steps.text:
The Security Council,

Reaffirming the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations,

Recalling the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on their Destruction of 1972,

Reaffirming that the use, development, production, acquisition, stockpiling, or retention of biological weapons constitutes a threat to international peace and security,

Emphasizing the importance of full compliance with the Convention by all States Parties,

Stressing the need for all States Parties to resolve any concerns regarding compliance through consultation and cooperation in accordance with the Convention,

Stressing the need for all States Parties to consider any allegations of non-compliance impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, and to uphold the authority of the Convention,

Recalling that the Convention provides the appropriate framework for addressing compliance concerns, including through Article V consultations, while reaffirming the Security Council's primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security under the Charter of the United Nations,

Welcoming the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties to the Convention,

1. Calls upon all States Parties to the Convention to fully comply with their obligations under the Convention;

2. Encourages all States Parties to engage in bilateral and multilateral consultations to resolve any concerns regarding compliance with the Convention, in accordance with Article V of the Convention, including, as appropriate, through a consultative meeting of States Parties;

3. Reaffirms that the Ninth Review Conference of the States Parties to the Convention is an appropriate forum to consider issues of compliance and verification, and that consideration of this matter by the Security Council is without prejudice to the work of the Review Conference and to the procedures set out in the Convention;

4. Affirms that nothing in this resolution shall be construed to limit or prejudge the Security Council's authority under the Charter of the United Nations to address threats to international peace and security, including alleged non-compliance with the Convention;

5. Decides to remain seized of the matter.

before.Albania: Albania supports full compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention and the strengthening of its implementation. At the same time, allegations must be handled impartially and on the basis of facts, and this Council must not be drawn into politically motivated disinformation. Because our proposed language against politicization and unfounded accusations was not retained, Albania will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.Brazil: Brazil thanks the President. Brazil remains fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to the prohibition of biological and toxin weapons. We support the draft’s reaffirmation of the Convention and its emphasis that compliance concerns should be addressed through cooperation under Article V and the Ninth Review Conference. Brazil will therefore vote in favour, without prejudice to our position that any allegations of non-compliance must be examined impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, and without substituting the Security Council for the Convention’s own procedures.
before.China: China will vote in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. The Biological Weapons Convention is a cornerstone of international security, and its authority must be upheld. China believes that concerns regarding compliance should be addressed impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, through the mechanisms provided by the Convention, including Article V consultations, and by the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference. The Security Council should support, not prejudge or politicize, the work of the Convention. The draft resolution is balanced and non-targeted, and China supports its adoption.
before.France: France votes in favour of this draft resolution. The Biological Weapons Convention is an essential instrument for international peace and security, and we fully support the call for all States Parties to comply with their obligations. We stress the importance of transparency, cooperation and the authority of the Ninth Review Conference, while reaffirming the Security Council’s role in addressing threats to international peace and security. France encourages all States Parties to resolve compliance concerns through the Convention’s procedures and in good faith.
before.Ghana: Ghana remains fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention, to full compliance by all States Parties, and to the Ninth Review Conference as an important forum for addressing compliance and verification. We regret that our proposed balanced and non-discriminatory mechanism for clarification of allegations of non-compliance was not retained in the text. Because the draft should have provided for a more impartial, transparent and fact-based process in line with the Convention, Ghana will abstain on this resolution.
before.India: India has consistently supported the Biological Weapons Convention and the full and effective implementation of all its provisions. We remain of the view that concerns relating to compliance must be considered impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, without politicization or double standards, including through the Convention’s Article V procedures and the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference. While the draft contains elements we can support, it does not fully reflect our proposed emphasis in the operative part. India will therefore abstain on the draft resolution.
before.Ireland:
Mr President,

Ireland remains fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to the Convention’s central role in addressing concerns about compliance. We take seriously all allegations of non-compliance, but they must be examined impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, in accordance with the Convention’s own procedures and in a manner that upholds its authority.

Ireland engaged constructively on this draft. We proposed a mechanism by which the Secretary-General could seek clarification from all States Parties concerned, without prejudice to Articles V and VI and without creating a parallel compliance process. We regret that this proposal was not taken up. For that reason, and because we remain concerned that this text risks politicising the Convention’s procedures and prejudging work properly belonging to the Ninth Review Conference, Ireland will abstain.
before.Norway: Norway remains fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to full compliance by all States Parties. We support transparent, fact-based efforts to resolve compliance concerns, but we abstain on this draft: it does not provide a credible or balanced response to the serious concerns before the Council and risks politicizing the Ninth Review Conference. Norway believes the Convention’s own mechanisms and the forthcoming Review Conference are the appropriate place to address these matters.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution submitted by our delegation. The text is balanced, depoliticized and aimed at strengthening the Biological Weapons Convention. It creates no new mechanisms; it calls on all States Parties to fully comply with their obligations and to resolve any concerns through Article V consultations, while preserving the Security Council’s prerogatives under the Charter. We regret attempts to politicize this issue and call on all members to support the authority of the Convention and the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference.
before.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates remains firmly committed to full compliance with the Biological Weapons Convention and to strengthening the Convention as a key pillar of international peace and security. We believe that concerns regarding compliance should be addressed through the Convention’s established procedures, transparent dialogue, and the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference, in which all States Parties can participate on an equal footing. While we support efforts to uphold the Convention, we are concerned that the current process risks deepening divisions within the Council and could undermine consensus-based work on this important issue. For these reasons, the United Arab Emirates abstains.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr. President. The United Kingdom will vote against this draft resolution. We remain fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to strengthening its implementation. But this text is not a genuine contribution to that goal. It is a distraction driven by the Russian Federation’s disinformation campaign, and it seeks to misuse the Security Council. Serious compliance concerns should be addressed through the Convention’s proper processes, including the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference, not through a politically motivated initiative in this Council. We therefore cannot support this draft and urge other members to reject it.
before.United States of America: The United States is fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to the peaceful uses of biological science. We reject Russia’s baseless allegations concerning biological weapons activities in Ukraine. This draft resolution is not a good-faith effort to strengthen the Convention; it is a political diversion designed to distract the Council from Russia’s own violations and to undermine the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference. While we appreciate some textual adjustments, the fundamental problems remain. The appropriate forum for compliance concerns is the BWC review process, not a politically motivated Security Council resolution. The United States will vote against this draft.

after.Gabon: Mr. President, Gabon abstained on the draft resolution before the Council. Our position is rooted in our full commitment to the Biological Weapons Convention and to the prohibition of biological and toxin weapons. Gabon supports full compliance by all States Parties with their obligations. At the same time, we believe that any allegations or concerns regarding non-compliance must be examined impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, including through the Convention’s own procedures, Article V consultations and the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference. Our abstention reflects our concern that the Security Council should not be drawn into a politicized or divisive exercise that could undermine consensus-based work on this important instrument. We encourage all States Parties to resolve concerns through dialogue and cooperation, and we reaffirm the Council’s responsibility to address threats to international peace and security without substituting for the Convention’s own mechanisms.
after.Kenya:
Mr President,

Kenya takes the floor to explain its abstention. Kenya is fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to the prohibition of biological and toxin weapons. We support full compliance by all States Parties and the strengthening of the Convention as a pillar of international peace and security.

Kenya believes that concerns regarding non-compliance are serious and must be addressed impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, in accordance with the Convention’s own procedures, including Article V, and through the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference. The Security Council has a role under the Charter, but it should not substitute for or politicize the Convention’s processes.

Kenya abstained because the draft before us, while containing elements we support, did not provide a sufficiently balanced and impartial mechanism for clarification of concerns, and it risked deepening divisions in the Council and around the Review Conference. We would have preferred a text that clearly supported a fact-based, cooperative process applicable to all States Parties in a non-discriminatory manner.

Kenya’s abstention does not diminish our commitment to the Convention. We urge all States Parties to pursue dialogue in good faith and to use the forthcoming Review Conference to strengthen compliance and verification.

Thank you.
after.Mexico:
Mr. President,

Mexico abstained on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. Mexico is fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to the prohibition of biological and toxin weapons in all circumstances. We believe that all States Parties must comply fully with their obligations and that any allegation of non-compliance must be examined impartially, transparently and on the basis of facts, through the Convention’s established procedures, including Article V consultations and the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference.

Mexico supported the draft’s reaffirmation of the Convention and its call for full compliance. However, we were not in a position to vote in favour of the text as presented. In Mexico’s view, the draft did not provide a sufficiently balanced and fact-based response to the serious concerns that have been raised, nor did it adequately reflect the need to avoid the politicization of the Convention and of the Security Council’s agenda. Mexico remains convinced that the authority of the Biological Weapons Convention and the integrity of its review process must be preserved.

Mexico therefore abstained, without prejudice to our firm support for the Convention and for international efforts to strengthen its implementation, including verification and compliance. We call on all States Parties to engage in good faith and to use the Ninth Review Conference to strengthen the Convention and to foster cooperation, transparency and confidence.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by our delegation. We regret that the Council has failed to adopt it. The text was balanced, non-confrontational and did not create any new mechanisms. It simply called on all States Parties to the Biological Weapons Convention to comply with their obligations and to resolve concerns through the Convention’s own procedures, including Article V consultations and the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference. It is difficult to understand how such a text could be presented as a threat to the authority of the Convention.

We thank the delegations that supported the draft. We also note that many members chose to abstain. In several cases this was not because the text contained anything they could reasonably reject, but because an atmosphere of pressure, disinformation and geopolitical confrontation was deliberately created by Washington and London. Those who abstained should not allow the BWC to become hostage to those who wish to avoid any impartial discussion of compliance.

The vote of the United States and the United Kingdom is revealing. It confirms that their real aim is not to strengthen the Convention, but to prevent the Security Council from considering compliance concerns, including the facts we have repeatedly presented about biological activities funded by the United States on Ukrainian territory. The accusations against Russia are false and are themselves part of a disinformation campaign. We categorically reject them.

The Russian Federation remains fully committed to the Biological Weapons Convention and to strengthening it, including through the elaboration of an effective verification mechanism. We will continue to raise this matter in the Security Council and at the Ninth Review Conference. We call on all States Parties to uphold the Convention impartially, without double standards, and to work on the basis of facts and mutual respect. The non-adoption of this draft does not remove the issue from the Council’s agenda or relieve us of our responsibility to maintain international peace and security.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States voted against this draft resolution, and we welcome the Council’s rejection of it. As we said before the vote, this text was never a genuine effort to strengthen the Biological Weapons Convention. It was a political diversion designed to distract this Council from Russia’s own violations and to undermine the forthcoming Ninth Review Conference.

The United States remains fully committed to the BWC and to the peaceful uses of biological science. We reject Russia’s baseless allegations concerning biological weapons activities in Ukraine. The appropriate forum for compliance concerns is the Convention’s own review process, including the Ninth Review Conference, not a politically motivated resolution in this Council.

We will continue to engage constructively with all States Parties to uphold and strengthen the Convention. We urge all members to focus on real threats to international peace and security and to avoid the misuse of this Council for disinformation.
